questions.stem: Immediately after the ship anchors, what must the officer of the watch do about the ship's position?
options: Fix and plot it promptly, then check often by bearings
Nothing more, since the anchor now holds the ship in place
Take one position at the end of the watch for the log book
Plot it only if the master asks for it on the bridge
questions.explanation: The anchor watch duty is to plot the position promptly and check frequently with bearings. A single check at the end of the watch is not "frequent".

questions.stem: During the anchor watch the bearings to two marks start changing steadily and the wind is rising. What must happen?
options: Nothing; the chain will hold her
Call the master only if the visibility also starts to drop
The officer waits until morning to check it against the chart
Notify the master: the anchor may be dragging
questions.explanation: The principles say to notify the master if the anchor drags, and also if visibility deteriorates. Changing bearings are the warning sign.

questions.stem: A watch and look-out continue at anchor and in port as well as at sea. Which list matches the duties of an anchor watch?
options: Check the passenger list, set radar to long range, sleep when the master is aboard
Run the main engine at sea speed and leave the bridge unattended
Fix and check position, look-out, rounds, weather, tide, lights, pollution
Sound the whistle hourly, paint the hull and wash down the deck
questions.explanation: These are the duties the watchkeeping principles list for an anchor watch. The other lists are unrelated or unsafe.

questions.stem: At 2200 bearings to marks A and B are 040 and 120. At 2300 they are 046 and 112, with the wind having risen. What is the best report and action?
options: Heave up the anchor at once without telling anyone on board
Report the 6 and 8 degree change at once: she may be dragging
Report nothing, because a change of 6 degrees is within normal error
Wait another hour to be sure before saying anything
questions.explanation: The bearings have moved, which means the ship is probably moving over the bottom. A steady bearing means holding. Report at once; the officer decides what to do and calls the master.

questions.stem: On a drift lead (a weighted line on the bottom), which sign suggests the anchor is dragging?
options: The line comes taut and leads well forward
The line lies slack and hangs straight down
The line has tangled itself round the chain
The line is wet when it is hauled in
questions.explanation: A line with no slack that tends noticeably forward means the ship is moving over the bottom, so the bridge must be told. A slack line hanging straight down is normal.

questions.stem: A 65 m vessel is anchored. Which description of her lights and day shape is correct?
options: Two red lights in a vertical line; by day three balls in a line
A single all-round green light; by day a black cylinder
No lights are needed at all inside a charted anchorage
All-round white forward, lower white aft; one ball by day
questions.explanation: Rule 30 requires a forward white all-round light and a lower stern white light for vessels of 50 m and over (one light is enough under 50 m), and one ball by day. Two red lights and three balls mean aground.

questions.stem: A mooring line is under heavy strain and a deckhand steps inside a loop of line on the deck to coil it. What is wrong?
options: Nothing; only standing right on the bow is ever dangerous
Nothing, but coiling should only be done at night
Never stand in a bight or snap-back zone of a loaded line
Nothing, because properly made-up lines never part
questions.explanation: Guidance says to keep out of snap-back zones and never stand in a bight of rope or wire. The zone grows round roller fairleads.

questions.stem: Which statement about communications for a bulk oil transfer is correct?
options: Only hand signals are allowed between ship and shore
Continuous two-way voice able to order an immediate shutdown
A single radio check at the start of the transfer is enough
Communication is needed only if the transfer lasts over 6 hours
questions.explanation: The regulation requires continuing two-way voice communication able to order immediate shutdown, and the duty person watches the tanks for overflow and keeps contact. One check at the start does not meet it.

questions.stem: An oil transfer is carried out after sunset. What lighting is required?
options: At least 54 lx at connections and 11 lx at work areas
At least 11 lx at connections and 54 lx at work areas
At least 100 lx everywhere on the deck and dock
No minimum is set, as long as torches are carried
questions.explanation: The regulation sets not less than 54 lx at each transfer connection point and not less than 11 lx at each work area around it. The values are not swapped.

questions.stem: During a fuel transfer a connection starts to leak. What do the supervisors have to do?
options: Keep pumping at full rate to finish the transfer quickly
Tighten the connection while it is still under pressure
Wait for the next watch to come on and deal with it
Slow or stop the transfer to take the pressure off
questions.explanation: A leak at a conduit or connection means the supervisors must slow down or stop the transfer to remove the pressure. Continuing at full rate is exactly what the regulation forbids.
